a.headline: How AI has exposed the cracks in the creative industry
a.summary: A new report by MikeTeevee reveals that many anxieties triggered by AI in creative agencies were actually pre-existing structural problems waiting to surface. For design students entering the industry, this is essential reading on how AI is reshaping studio culture, workflows, and creative value.

a.headline: Sekondo Puts ChatGPT and Claude Inside After Effects and Premiere Pro
a.summary: A new plugin called Sekondo integrates large language models directly into six Adobe applications, including After Effects and Premiere Pro, changing how motion designers can script, edit, and iterate. If you work in motion design, this is a practical look at how AI assistance is embedding itself into the tools you already use.

a.headline: Oh, Apple Music has a new logo. We talk with Curtis Free about why the making matters more in an AI world.
a.summary: Apple Music has rebranded using a physical process -- sound waves passed through mineral oil -- and Design Week uses this as a launching point to ask why craft and process feel so important to communicate right now. The conversation with Curtis Free is a timely one for designers thinking about how to position handmade process as a value in an AI-saturated landscape.

a.headline: Just Eat's AI apocalypse raises a glaring question
a.summary: Just Eat has deployed AI-generated content at scale, and the results are prompting serious questions about quality, brand trust, and the role of human creative judgment. This is a useful case study for students thinking about where AI adoption in commercial design risks going wrong.

b.headline: AI's hidden storage bill: What inference leaves behind
b.summary: Beyond the well-known energy cost of training AI models, this piece exposes the massive and often overlooked storage infrastructure required every time a model is actually used at scale. For designers using generative tools daily, it is a sobering reminder that every prompt carries an invisible environmental price tag.

b.headline: Meta announces $95bn fundraising drive to pay for AI expansion
b.summary: Meta is raising nearly $100 billion to fund continued AI infrastructure build-out, signalling the extraordinary scale of capital -- and by extension energy and resources -- being committed to AI expansion globally. Understanding the financial and physical infrastructure behind the tools designers use puts their environmental cost in sharper focus.

c.headline: Inside Robin Hunter Blake's stroboscopic photography
c.summary: Photographer and filmmaker Robin Hunter Blake has built an atmospheric practice rooted in historical stroboscopic techniques, deliberately choosing slow, process-driven methods over digital convenience. His work is a compelling example of how deep engagement with analogue technology can produce images that feel genuinely distinct from AI-generated visual culture.

c.headline: Michelle Gruppetta's riso-printed animation reveals what sound sensitivity actually feels like
c.summary: Maltese animator Michelle Gruppetta made her debut short Misophonia by combining risograph printing with animation, using a deliberately labour-intensive and physically grounded process to communicate an experience that defies easy digital rendering. The work is a strong case for how material constraint and slow-tech methods can produce emotional specificity that generative tools struggle to replicate.

c.headline: Anthropic sued for allegedly using 274 Elvis Presley songs to train AI models
c.summary: The owners of Elvis Presley's music catalogue are suing Anthropic for allegedly using hundreds of his songs without permission to train Claude, adding to a growing wave of intellectual property litigation targeting AI companies. For design and illustration students, this case is directly relevant to ongoing debates about whether creative work scraped for training data constitutes theft.

c.headline: Dear ChatGPT: 12-year-old wins top youth prize at Australian Poetry Slam
c.summary: A 12-year-old named Blake Mackenzie won a national poetry competition with a piece addressed directly to ChatGPT, using the oldest human expressive form to interrogate the newest machine intelligence. It is a striking reminder that critical engagement with AI does not require a studio or a screen -- sometimes a voice and a stage are enough.
